statement: Slack container design rationale: The original Slack container design treated the container as a top-level virtual thread to accommodate both main messages and threaded replies under unified thread_id grouping

subject: container-scope to thread-scope fact duplication

subject: thread-scope watermark calculation design
statement: thread-scope watermark calculation design: Watermark should be calculated from thread_scope_facts only and ignore container-scope watermarks, so the first thread-scope run processes the full thread from scratch rather than relying on the preliminary container-scope extraction watermark

subject: thread-scope LLM context strategy
statement: thread-scope LLM context strategy: LLM context should still include all existing facts (both container-scope and thread-scope) so the LLM is aware and can avoid exact re-extraction, even though watermark calculation ignores container-scope facts

subject: standalone messages in container-scope
statement: Standalone messages remain in container-scope forever because no thread-scope extraction ever fires for them, making them unaffected by the watermark separation fix

subject: thread-scope extraction on first run
statement: thread-scope extraction on first run: First thread-scope run produces near-duplicate facts in different wording from container-scope preliminary facts because thread-scope skips message 1 via watermark but messages 2+ reference the same content, and exact-match dedup cannot catch paraphrases

subject: container-scope + thread-scope extraction sequencing
statement: container-scope + thread-scope extraction sequencing: Container-scope processes single-message threads immediately because thread-scope needs 2+ messages to run, creating preliminary facts with thread_ref=None that later become duplicates when thread-scope fires

subject: thread-scope watermark strategy on first run
statement: thread-scope watermark strategy on first run: Ignoring watermark from container-scope facts on thread-scope's first run allows full-thread reprocessing with better context, replacing preliminary facts rather than producing incremental duplicates

subject: Container-scope and thread-scope fact extraction
statement: Container-scope and thread-scope fact extraction: Supersession semantics as initially proposed were incorrect because thread-scope extraction produces different facts from fuller context, not replacements of container-scope facts, and semantic matching to pair them would be disproportionately complex

subject: Watermark-only fix for duplicate facts
statement: Watermark-only fix for duplicate facts: Ignoring container-scope watermarks to let thread-scope re-process message 1 does not eliminate the duplicate because the container-scope fact still remains active alongside whatever thread-scope produces

subject: Thread-scope extraction with full context
statement: Thread-scope extraction with full context: Thread-scope is strictly superior to container-scope extraction because thread-scope sees all messages including message 1, and if a container-scope fact was valid the LLM will re-extract it with richer context; if it doesn't re-extract it, the fact wasn't worth keeping

subject: Unconditional supersession approach for container-scope facts

subject: LLM context strategy during thread-scope supersession
statement: LLM context strategy during thread-scope supersession: Passing all existing facts (container + thread) to LLM as context during thread-scope execution prevents exact re-extraction while allowing the LLM to re-extract with richer context or skip invalid container-scope facts

subject: First thread-scope run performance cost

subject: Race condition risk in container/thread-scope supersession
statement: Race condition risk in container/thread-scope supersession: Concurrent execution of thread-scope and container-scope on the same items could result in supersession of recently written container-scope facts, but this is mitigated by the lease mechanism which ensures only one scope runs at a time per plugin

subject: thread-scope execution strategy

subject: Atomic fact extraction prompt
statement: Atomic fact extraction prompt: Current prompt interpretation allows LLM to treat assistant's reasoning chains as 'stated' facts because prompt says 'record what participants stated' without explicitly excluding the assistant as a non-participant

subject: Atomic fact extraction pipeline
statement: Atomic fact extraction pipeline: 294 facts (51% of 575) categorized as 'event' include ephemeral conversation observations like API errors and session state changes that would never be retrievable for future queries, suggesting event category is being applied too broadly

subject: Deduplication in fact extraction
statement: Deduplication in fact extraction: Exact normalized (subject, statement) key matching misses paraphrases of the same constraint — four different phrasings of 'muxi should not be mentioned by name' all passed through as separate facts

subject: Atomic fact extraction filtering
statement: Atomic fact extraction filtering: 107 facts (19%) categorized as 'activity' are pure session narration (user requested X, user wants to understand Y) that lack durable knowledge and would not satisfy future relevance queries

subject: Atomic fact extraction improvements
statement: Atomic fact extraction improvements: Recent prompt changes successfully reduced grab-bag 'User' subject bucket from 240 to 18 facts, and interest over-extraction was resolved by token gate and classification changes dropping volume from flood to 3 items, demonstrating that prompt engineering can substantially reduce noise

subject: Fact extraction prompt handling of meta-conversation
statement: Fact extraction prompt handling of meta-conversation: The extraction prompt has a systemic weakness: when assistant messages contain both validation frames and substantive content, the LLM extracts the validation frame ('it's solid') instead of the actionable findings, treating meta-statements about the conversation as domain findings

subject: Investigation outcome vector indexing

subject: Investigation outcome extraction failure mode
statement: Investigation outcome extraction failure mode: The extraction process selects the first summary-looking sentence from source material, causing headings and meta-statements to be captured as investigation_outcome field even when substantive findings appear in the body text

subject: Investigation outcome vector indexing
statement: Investigation outcome vector indexing: Vector embeddings for generic investigation outcomes like 'Root Causes Found' or meta-verdicts like 'The 4 problems are real' cluster into generic 'conclusion/validation' regions and fail to match queries about actual topics, while lexical search partially compensates through evidence field keywords but suffers precision loss from noisy concatenated FTS blob

subject: Investigation outcome extraction quality
statement: Investigation outcome extraction quality: Investigation outcome field prioritization causes generic titles and meta-assessments to dominate the primary vector retrieval surface (200-400 char summary + rationale) while actionable findings remain confined to evidence_text which is a secondary lexical-only lookup

subject: Pallium embedding configuration defaults
statement: Pallium embedding configuration defaults: Defaults should not be specified in the config file; the config file is only for optional changes, so the default embedding model should be a code default rather than a config entry

subject: Vector similarity thresholds in Pallium
statement: Vector similarity thresholds in Pallium: Similarity thresholds should be attached to the selected embedding model rather than hardcoded as generic numbers, because similarity distributions are model-dependent

subject: Pallium embedding model migration
statement: Changing the embedding model in running Pallium services raises unresolved questions about service startup behavior, model version detection, and migration strategy that need to be addressed
